metadata.title: A job-search agent that shows its evidence
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: I narrate as myself (Nishant), so the persona bookends are dropped: no Liam/Bear greeting, no composer cold open, no verdict card, no Your Turn. The ClaudeTitleOutro (BOUT) is also dropped because its handle is hard-coded to @NikBearBrown; the film closes on a drawn Manim beat, BEND. bookend_check.py's outro check cannot be exempted and will fail by design.

metadata.author: Nishant U

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Nee-shaant. I lost hours reading job postings that turned out to be a bad fit, or that never mentioned sponsorship. So the real question was which postings are worth my time.

show.event: types 'How do I find more job postings'
backspaces 'more job postings' → 'postings worth my time' on the spoken correction

props.text:
How do I find
more job postings

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive question and corrects it to the real one: which postings are worth my time.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. Two verdicts: a rule verdict anyone can recompute, kept beside Claude's judgment. Evidence labels: a claim will be supported only when the posting says it, and insufficient when it is silent. Human gate: I will approve the shortlist.

terms.meaning: a rule verdict anyone can recompute, beside Claude's judgment
supported only when the posting says it; insufficient when it is silent
I will approve the shortlist; nothing will be sent

beats.narration_text: I will build a job-search agent. It will watch public job boards at retail and e-commerce companies, and tell a fictional international data-analytics graduate which new postings are worth their time.

beats.narration_text: Every verdict will cite the posting text and resume field behind it. It will never apply or send anything. The repo will hold a Python agent, tests, an evaluation log, a ten-document evidence packet, and a five-minute demo.

beats.narration_text: I looked at two tools I had used. LinkedIn Job Alerts emailed me postings that matched a saved search, but never told me why a job fit me, or whether it mentioned sponsorship.

shot.visual_intent: A generic envelope shape (no logo) drops postings onto the stage; a blank tag swings beside each posting where a reason would be.

beats.narration_text: Jobright went further: a match score, an H one B filter, and an agent that could submit applications. But a 2026 careery dot pro review said its filter used sponsorship language or past sponsorship history, which doesn't guarantee this job will sponsor.

shot.visual_intent: A generic dial-and-funnel machine (no logo): a needle swings (score), postings pass a funnel (filter); a history ledger page feeds the funnel from behind.
shot.motion_claim: A generic dial-and-funnel machine (no logo): a needle swings (score), postings pass a funnel (filter); a history ledger page feeds the funnel from behind.

beats.narration_text: Mine will differ in three ways. It will judge each posting by its own text, and quote the line. When a posting is silent, it will say insufficient instead of guessing. And it will never apply. I will approve the shortlist.

shot.visual_intent: One posting page; a quote bracket draws around one line and a check lands (supported); a blank stretch gets an open ring (insufficient); a send arrow is stopped at a gate.

beats.narration_text: A hiring manager for data analyst, data scientist, or analytics engineer roles will open the read-me and run one command on saved board data. In sixty seconds they will see the shortlist with citations, skipped postings with reasons, and the scorecard.

shot.visual_intent: A laptop on a desk (no person); a command line types, then three trays slide out: shortlist (pages with ticks), skipped (pages with reason tags), scorecard (bar block).

beats.narration_text: It will prove prompt contracts with a validator, and a rule verdict beside Claude's judgment. An agent loop with budgets, exits, and a stop that doesn't rely on the model. Permissions in code, versioned memory, and a human gate tied to the exact shortlist.

shot.visual_intent: The agent block on a loop track; a budget meter drains as it laps; an exit gate opens at a fixed lap and the block stops; a padlock sits on a tool port.

beats.narration_text: The evidence will be tests, a held-out evaluation with at least five deliberate failure cases, a controlled failure I will predict and then trigger, and a stranger's run of the read-me.

shot.visual_intent: A test sheet with checks; an evaluation sheet beside it with five marked failure rows; one ink cross lands on the predicted row.

beats.narration_text: It will never apply, email, message, or log in, and it won't scrape LinkedIn. First: one public board and one fictional resume. The first run will be a baseline with zero new postings. The proof: the saved raw board response and the state file.

beats.narration_text: The risk: many postings never state sponsorship or pay, so the agent could look confident with nothing behind it. The fix will be an insufficient label, an abstention rule, and measuring how often it abstains.

shot.visual_intent: A posting page with blank lines; a tall check grows over it with nothing under it, then is replaced by an open-ring tag; a small gauge needle rises (abstain rate).

beats.narration_text: Why this project? Showing off and learning. I bring Python, SQL, and data analysis from almost two years as a Data Analyst at Deloitte, and a co-op at Wayfair. New to me will be agent loops with budgets, permissions in code, an MCP server from scratch, and an evaluation that can say no.
